# Control Narrative: Ammonia Screw Compressor C-101

**Doc status:** DRAFT for owner review. Values in **[brackets]** are my proposed defaults, not from the process data. Confirm or replace them before issue (see Section 12).

## 1. Scope and Equipment

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| C-101 | Ammonia screw compressor, 400 hp, slide valve capacity control 10-100% |
| Starter | Across-the-line soft starter (no VFD) |
| Controller | Allen-Bradley CompactLogix PLC |
| HMI | Engine room office |
| PT-101 | Suction pressure transmitter |
| PDT-102 | Oil differential pressure transmitter |
| TT-103 | Discharge temperature transmitter |
| II-104 | Motor current transmitter (CT input), % FLA |
| AE-110A/B | Machine room ammonia detectors |
| EF-201 | Emergency exhaust fan, high speed |
| XV-120 | Machine room main liquid solenoid valve |
| ESD-PB | Hardwired break-glass emergency stop station, outside the machine room |

This narrative covers C-101 control, protection and ammonia-release response. Other machine room equipment is out of scope except where it is shut down by the ammonia response.

## 2. General Requirements

1. **Hardwired ESD.** The break-glass station is wired in the safety/power circuit so it de-energizes the C-101 starter and XV-120 independent of PLC state. The PLC also reads it as an input for alarm and annunciation only.
2. **Fail-safe outputs.** XV-120 is energized to open and spring-closes on loss of power or signal. Trips are de-energize-to-trip.
3. **Latched trips.** All trips latch. Reset requires the condition to be clear and a manual reset at the HMI (the ammonia 150 ppm and ESD resets are defined in Section 8).
4. **Analog fault handling.** Any trip or control analog reading outside 3.8-20.5 mA is flagged as bad quality. Bad quality on PT-101, PDT-102 or TT-103 raises an instrument-fault alarm and **[trips C-101 if running, and blocks start]**. Bad quality on II-104 blocks loading and raises an alarm.
5. **Authority.** Operator login can start/stop, select mode and reset. Supervisor login is required to change setpoints, alarm and trip limits, and the start-count limit. Trip limits are shown on the HMI but are not changeable by operators.

## 3. Operating Modes

- **Off:** C-101 stopped, start blocked.
- **Manual:** Operator starts/stops C-101 and pulses the slide valve load/unload from the HMI. All protective functions remain active, including the 95% FLA load inhibit.
- **Auto:** C-101 slide valve is controlled on PT-101 per Section 5. **[Auto start/stop on suction pressure is not in scope unless the owner adds a sequencing requirement.]**

## 4. Start Sequence

### 4.1 Start Permissives
All must be true, or the start command is rejected and the first-out reason is displayed:

1. No active latched trip, and ESD-PB healthy (not pressed).
2. Machine room ammonia below 150 ppm (no active ammonia shutdown).
3. PT-101 above the 2 psig low trip, with good signal quality.
4. TT-103 and PDT-102 signals good.
5. Slide valve at **[minimum position, ≤10%]**. If not, the PLC unloads first and the start is held until it is.
6. Start count in the last rolling 60 minutes is below 4 (Section 4.3).
7. Soft starter reports ready/no fault.

### 4.2 Start Steps
1. Operator issues start command. The PLC re-verifies permissives.
2. PLC energizes the soft starter run command.
3. The 30 s low-oil-pressure trip bypass timer starts at the moment the motor run command is issued.
4. Motor runs. Soft starter run-feedback must be received within **[5 s]**, otherwise the PLC records a "failed to start" trip.
5. The slide valve is held at minimum for **[10 s]** after run feedback, then released to Auto control (or Manual).
6. At 30 s the bypass expires and the low-oil trip is armed.

### 4.3 Starts-per-Hour Limit
The PLC counts starts in a rolling 60 min window. After 4 starts in the window, a fifth start is blocked, "Start inhibit: max starts/hr" is shown, and the time remaining until the oldest start ages out is displayed. A start is counted when the run command is issued, regardless of whether the start succeeds. The counter persists through PLC power cycles (retentive). Stop and trip actions are never blocked by this limit.

## 5. Capacity Control (Auto)

- **Process variable:** PT-101 suction pressure.
- **Setpoint:** 15 psig, adjustable 5-30 psig by supervisor login. The input is range-limited in the PLC, and out-of-range entries are rejected with a message.
- **Action:** Slide valve loads when PT-101 is above setpoint and unloads when below, using pulsed load/unload outputs.
- **Method:** Pulse width and interval are proportional to error outside a deadband. Proposed starting values: deadband **[±0.5 psi]**, minimum pulse **[0.5 s]**, maximum pulse **[3 s]**, minimum interval between pulses **[5-30 s, scaled by error]**. All are supervisor-adjustable and tuned at commissioning.
- **Limits:** Load pulses are never issued if the slide valve is at 100%. Unload pulses are never issued at 10%. Slide valve position is displayed from the position feedback. **[Assumes a position transmitter exists; if not, position is estimated by pulse time and must be flagged as estimated.]**
- **Fixed output exclusivity:** Load and unload outputs can never be on at the same time.
- **Suction-pressure approach to low trip:** PT-101 below **[setpoint minus 3 psi, floored at 4 psig]** forces unload pulses regardless of the deadband (low suction unload). The 2 psig trip in Section 7 remains independent.

## 6. Motor Current Limit

- II-104 is scaled to % of motor FLA. The FLA value is a supervisor-entered constant (nameplate).
- **At ≥95% FLA:** Load pulses are inhibited in both Auto and Manual, and "Current limit active" is displayed.
- **At ≥ [98% FLA] for more than [10 s]:** The PLC issues unload pulses until current falls below 95% (hysteresis: load inhibit clears at **[92%]**).
- This is a loading limit, not a trip. Motor overload and short-circuit protection remain with the soft starter and the motor circuit protection. Starting inrush is ignored by this function for **[30 s]** after the run command (the unload-on-overcurrent action only; the load inhibit stays active).

## 7. Protection: Alarms and Trips

| Tag | Condition | Alarm | Trip |
|---|---|---|---|
| PDT-102 | Low oil differential | <35 psid, **[5 s delay]** | <25 psid, **[5 s delay]**; bypassed for 30 s after start |
| TT-103 | High discharge temp | >190 °F, **[5 s delay]** | >210 °F, **[5 s delay]** |
| PT-101 | Low suction pressure | **[<4 psig]** | <2 psig, **[5 s delay]** |
| II-104 | High current | ≥95% FLA (load inhibit message, not a trip) | Soft starter overload |

Notes:
1. **Low-oil bypass applies only to the PDT-102 trip.** The PDT-102 alarm may still annunciate during the bypass window **[but is suppressed for the first 30 s to avoid nuisance alarms; owner to confirm]**. All other alarms and trips (TT-103, PT-101, ammonia, ESD) are active from the start command.
2. **PT-101 low trip** is bypassed for **[none]**. If the compressor cannot start without tripping on suction pressure at light load, a start bypass is a design change requiring owner approval.
3. **Trip action:** Remove the soft starter run command immediately, unload the slide valve to minimum if the motor is stopped (so the next start meets permissives), and latch first-out cause with timestamp on the HMI. Trip delays use the PLC timers listed above.
4. Alarm limits and trip limits are supervisor-editable only within enforced ordering (alarm must be on the safe side of trip).
5. Alarms clear automatically when the condition clears (with **[hysteresis 1 psi / 2 °F / 1 psid]**) and require acknowledgement. Trips need reset per Section 2.

## 8. Ammonia Detection and Emergency Response

### 8.1 25 ppm (alarm)
When either AE-110A or AE-110B reaches ≥25 ppm:
- Annunciate on the HMI and sound/flash the machine room beacon/horn **[if installed]**.
- Start EF-201 at **high speed** and latch it on until the reading is below 25 ppm on both detectors **[and a manual reset is done]**.
- C-101 continues to run.

### 8.2 150 ppm (shutdown)
When either detector reaches ≥150 ppm:
- Trip C-101 and all other machine room compressors (latched).
- De-energize XV-120 (closes).
- Keep EF-201 running at high speed.
- Annunciate "Ammonia emergency shutdown" and record the first-out.
- The 150 ppm shutdown is latched. Reset requires both readings below 25 ppm **[and a local manual reset by supervisor login]**.

### 8.3 Voting and Fault Assumption
**[Assumed 1-out-of-2 voting for both levels: either detector alone causes the action.]** Owner to confirm. A detector fault (bad signal, below 3.8 mA or above 20.5 mA) raises an alarm and is treated as **[a 25 ppm condition (EF-201 high)]**. If both detectors fail, treat as 150 ppm **[owner to confirm]**.

### 8.4 Break-Glass Emergency Shutdown
Pressing ESD-PB hardwire-removes C-101 starter power and XV-120 power independently of the PLC. The PLC detects the input, trips all compressors, latches "ESD activated", and starts EF-201 at high speed **[owner to confirm EF-201 behavior on manual ESD]**. Reset requires physically resetting the break-glass station, then an HMI reset.

### 8.5 Restart After Emergency
The XV-120 reopen and compressor restart are manual and deliberate. The PLC never auto-reopens XV-120 or auto-restarts after a latched ammonia or ESD event.

## 9. Stop Sequence

- **Normal stop:** Operator stop command → slide valve unloads to minimum (timeout **[120 s]**) → motor run command removed. Stop is permitted at any time and will not wait if a trip is active.
- **Trip or ESD stop:** Immediate removal of the run command (no unload wait).
- **Power loss:** C-101 stops. On power restoration, there is no auto-restart. The start-count history is retained.

## 10. HMI Requirements

1. Overview screen: C-101 status (running/stopped/tripped), mode, PT-101, setpoint, slide valve %, PDT-102, TT-103, II-104 %FLA, ammonia ppm (A and B), EF-201 and XV-120 states, start count and time to next permitted start.
2. First-out trip banner with timestamp and value.
3. Alarm summary with acknowledge, and alarm/event history (minimum **[30 days]**).
4. Supervisor-only setup screen for setpoints, limits, delays and FLA, with every change logged (user, old value, new value, time).
5. Start permissive screen showing each permissive as pass/fail.

## 11. FAT Test Procedure Summary

Simulate inputs by signal injection or forced test points. Each test records pass/fail, actual values and witness initials.

| # | Test | Method | Expected result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Start permissives | Defeat each permissive one at a time | Start rejected, correct reason shown |
| 2 | Low-oil bypass | Run with PDT-102 at 20 psid | No trip for 30 s (±1 s), trip after 30 s plus delay |
| 3 | Low-oil alarm/trip | Ramp PDT-102 down after 30 s | Alarm <35, trip <25 psid |
| 4 | High discharge temp | Ramp TT-103 up | Alarm >190 °F, trip >210 °F |
| 5 | Low suction | Ramp PT-101 down | Forced unload, alarm, trip <2 psig |
| 6 | Capacity control | PT-101 above/below setpoint | Load/unload pulses in correct direction, deadband respected, no simultaneous outputs |
| 7 | Setpoint range | Enter 4 and 31 psig, then 5 and 30 | 4 and 31 rejected, 5 and 30 accepted; operator login cannot change |
| 8 | Current limit | Inject II-104 at 94%, 95%, 98%+ | Load allowed at 94, inhibited at 95, unloads at 98%+ after delay |
| 9 | Starts per hour | Perform 4 starts, attempt a fifth | Fifth blocked, time remaining shown; verify retention through PLC power cycle |
| 10 | 25 ppm | Inject AE-110A, then AE-110B | Alarm, EF-201 high speed, C-101 keeps running |
| 11 | 150 ppm | Inject on each detector | All compressors trip, XV-120 de-energizes, EF-201 high, latched |
| 12 | Detector fault | Open loop on each detector | Alarm and defined response per 8.3 |
| 13 | Break-glass ESD | Press ESD-PB with PLC in run, then with PLC powered off | Starter and XV-120 drop out in both cases |
| 14 | Latching/reset | Clear each condition | Trips remain until the correct manual reset |
| 15 | Instrument failure | Wire break on PT-101, PDT-102, TT-103, II-104 | Alarm and defined action per Section 2 |
| 16 | Power cycle | Cycle PLC power while running and tripped | No auto-restart, trips and counters per design |

## 12. Open Items for Owner Confirmation

1. Detector voting (1oo2 assumed) and detector-fault response.
2. Whether EF-201 starts on manual ESD, and whether its 25 ppm latch needs a manual reset.
3. Whether slide valve position feedback exists.
4. Whether a suction-pressure trip delay or start bypass is acceptable.
5. All bracketed values: delays, hysteresis, pulse timing, unload-on-overcurrent threshold, and instrument-fault trip behavior.
6. Ancillaries not described and not covered here: oil pump, oil cooling, liquid injection, condenser/evaporator interlocks, and auto start/stop sequencing between compressors.
7. Applicable code basis (for example IIAR 2/9 and local requirements) to be cited by the engineer of record. I have not verified the detector setpoints against them.
8. Motor FLA nameplate value and soft starter model, for the current scaling and overload settings.
